capture.final_message:
Prove the outer conjunction by treating the two equivalences independently. In each equivalence, both sides are standard categorical facts, so prove both propositions outright rather than trying to transform one into the other.

- For binary products, use the defining characterization of `PreservesLimitPair.iso`: its inverse followed by the image of either product projection is the corresponding projection in the target. The required equality is precisely the second-projection compatibility.

- For binary coproducts, an invertible `coprodComparison` identifies the image of the chosen coproduct cocone with the target coproduct cocone. Transporting the colimit property across this isomorphism yields `PreservesColimit` for the discrete walking pair.

- For the adjunction statement, use that a left adjoint preserves colimits. The converse relies essentially on the right adjoint being full and faithful: the counit is then an isomorphism, so colimits in the reflective category `D` can be represented by applying `F` to colimits in `C`. Hence `H` preserves `J`-colimits exactly when `F ⋙ H` does.

- For the initial-object statement, view an initial object as the colimit of the empty diagram. If `initialComparison` is invertible, the image under `G` of the chosen initial object is isomorphic to the chosen initial object of `D`, and therefore is initial; this gives preservation of the empty colimit.

The useful intermediate goals are thus the two comparison-isomorphism criteria—one for binary (co)products and one for the empty colimit—and the fully faithful right-adjoint characterization of colimits in `D`.
